title: Redwood data retention & PII controls demo - Sable Payments
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Sable Payments through console and API controls for data handling: per-route request storage toggles, automatic PII redaction, retention windows (30/90/365 days), KMS-encrypted at-rest storage, and private deployment options. Customer cares about SOC2, SSO, immediate purge and legal hold. Next steps: send security pack, pricing, and schedule pilot for request-storage off testing.
next_steps: Maya to send SOC 2 + security whitepaper and KMS architecture diagram by 2026-04-13
Rafael to share short demo recording + console screenshots of retention toggle by 2026-04-12
Schedule 2-week pilot to test store_request=false and automated redaction - target start 2026-04-20
action_items: Maya Chen - Send SOC2 + security whitepaper - 2026-04-13
Rafael Ortiz - Export console screenshots of 'Data Retention' and 'Redaction Rules' - 2026-04-12
Aisha Khan - Confirm pilot scope & internal POC owners - 2026-04-16
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'll do a quick run through of our data handling controls and Rafael will do console demo.
[00:10] Priya Singh: Thanks, Maya. Quick ask on the top 

we're PCI scoped and SOC 2, we need to understand storage, purge, and PII redaction.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Absolutely. High level: managed hosted API by default stores request/response for 30 days for debugging, but you can toggle per-route store_request/store_response to false via API or Console. You can also set retention windows to 30/90/365 or custom on Dedicated/Private.
[00:38] Liam O'Connor: Where does stored data live? Is it encrypted with our KMS?
[00:44] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, at-rest encryption using AES-256 and customer-managed KMS in private deployments; we integrate with AWS KMS or HSM for Dedicated. For hosted we use Redwood-managed keys but we offer bring-your-own-KMS in Private.
[01:02] Priya Singh: And audit logs / who accessed what? We need proof for audits.
[01:07] Maya Chen: Console has an Audit Logs view, and you can export logs or stream to your SIEM. All access is tracked with SSO/SAML + RBAC. We keep an immutable audit trail; entries show redaction applied and who downloaded.
[01:25] Aisha Khan: Show us the UI for toggling storage 


are these per-route?
[01:30] Rafael Ortiz: Yep. I'll share my screen. On the route config you get toggles: 'Store requests' checkbox, 'Store responses' checkbox, and a retention dropdown.
[01:45] Rafael Ortiz: (screen) Here  


you can set "store_request": false in the API call too, example: POST /v1/generate {..., "store_request": false, "store_response": false}. That prevents persisting the raw payload into long-term storage.
[02:05] Priya Singh: Does redaction happen before any logging? Like if someone copies logs to our SIEM are we safe?
[02:10] Rafael Ortiz: We run a two-step pipeline: first automated PII redaction (configurable regex and pattern matches) then hashing/tokenization. By default we redact obvious things: SSNs, credit card patterns, email addresses, phone numbers. You can add custom patterns via Console.
[02:30] Liam O'Connor: Is the redaction deterministic? If we do a legal hold, can we recover raw data?
[02:36] Maya Chen: If you have store_request on and no purge, raw is kept. For legal hold we can pause retention policies; however, if store_request was false at capture time, there's no raw to recover. So pilot will be important.
[02:55] Priya Singh: How about deletion / right-to-be-forgotten? API for deletion?
[02:59] Rafael Ortiz: Yes \u2014 delete endpoints exist. There's a delete-by-transaction-id and delete-by-customer-id. In Private we also support on-prem purge scripts. Deletion requests generate an audit event.
[03:15] Maya Chen: Also worth noting we support per-route redact rules and global redaction policy. You can choose to redact in logs but keep hashes for analytics.
[03:30] Aisha Khan: Is there any risk of model fine-tuning from stored customer prompts?
[03:35] Rafael Ortiz: We do not use customer data to improve models unless you opt in. No training on customer data in hosted by default. For enterprise contracts we can contractually guarantee no training.
[03:50] Liam O'Connor: What about data residency  

EU vs US?
[03:54] Maya Chen: Hosting regions are selectable; for hosted we can pin storage region, or you can use Private deployment for full control. For Dedicated we offer regional isolation.
[04:10] Priya Singh: Any SOC2/ISO certs and penetration test reports?
[04:14] Maya Chen: We'll send our SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summary in the security pack.
[04:20] Rafael Ortiz: Back to the console, here's the redaction rule builder: simple regex UI and a preview on sample payloads. The transcript may show some OCR issues 

s e g sometimes K M S is split 

[04:35] Priya Singh: (laughs) yeah smaller issue.
[04:40] Rafael Ortiz: For the API, examples: cURL: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer {key}' -d '{"input":"...","store_request":false, "retain_days":30}'. The retain_days param is honored unless you are on Dedicated or Private where custome policies apply.
[05:05] Liam O'Connor: If we set store_request false but keep store_response true, will metadata still be saved?
[05:12] Rafael Ortiz: We persist minimal metadata for billing and tracing 

like request id, model used, token counts. PII is not stored if the request body is not stored; but some metadata fields are non-PII.
[05:25] Priya Singh: We need to ensure token counts cannot be used to infer content 

is that a risk?
[05:30] Maya Chen: Token counts are numeric only; we can aggregate them and add noise if needed. Our Optimize tool recommends batching and caching, which affects token accounting, but we can customize reporting for audits.
[05:50] Aisha Khan: Can we integrate with our KMS to rotate keys?
[05:54] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, key rotation supported. In private deployments you manage the KMS and rotate keys on your schedule; Redwood supports automatic re-encryption flows.
[06:10] Liam O'Connor: For the pilot, we want to test the store_request=false path end-to-end with our webhook sink. Can you stream events to our SIEM?
[06:16] Maya Chen: Yes, we support streaming audit logs and anonymized event streams to customer S3 or to your syslog/Splunk. We'll work with your security team to set a secure forwarder.
[06:30] Priya Singh: Are there any gotchas where logs might leak into third-party tools? For example, debugging traces that are exported?
[06:36] Rafael Ortiz: Debug traces are opt-in and marked. When you enable debug for a route we also add a retention and explicit disclaimer; debug data is only stored if you enable it. We can enforce org-level policies to prevent devs from turning debug on in production.
[06:58] Liam O'Connor: About redaction quality  

false positives / negatives 

can we run the redaction engine on historical logs?
[07:04] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, we provide a one-time scrub job that can run against stored logs and apply updated rules. That job produces an audit trail showing changes.
[07:20] Aisha Khan: Great. Anything on legal hold and exportability?
[07:24] Maya Chen: Exports are supported. For legal hold we can snapshot and provide a secured export and then re-enable retention.
[07:35] Priya Singh: Will you include sample SLA language about data handling in the contract?
[07:39] Maya Chen: Yes, we can include data handling clauses 

non-training guarantee, retention terms, SOC2, and breach notification timelines.
[07:48] Liam O'Connor: Can we demo an API call that sets store_request false now?
[07:52] Rafael Ortiz: Sure, I'll run a quick cURL from my terminal. (typing) curl ... -d '{"input":"card 4111 1111 1111 1111", "store_request":false}' and you'll see response but request won't be stored. Note: in the transcription the sample CC number was redacted in the UI preview.
[08:15] Aisha Khan: Does redact run in real time or asynchronously?
[08:19] Rafael Ortiz: It runs inline and then additional scrub jobs can run asynchronously for older data.
[08:28] Priya Singh: Ok thanks. How do we ensure developers don't accidentally set store_request to true? We need guardrails.
[08:33] Rafael Ortiz: We have org-level policies and route templates that can lock settings; only org admins can change them. Also API keys can be scoped so junior dev keys cannot override storage settings.
[08:50] Maya Chen: Quick note on Dedicated vs Hosted: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and more control over retention/region; Private gives full control including BYO KMS and air-gapped installs. Hosted is fastest to get started but has some managed defaults.
[09:05] Liam O'Connor: Cost differences? If we store less data will that lower our bill?
[09:09] Maya Chen: Storage charges are modest relative to inference cost, but storing fewer tokens reduces long-term storage and egress. Optimize can recommend quantization and batching to cut token costs.
[09:25] Priya Singh: Ok could you send the pricing + estimate for a 6-month pilot with store_request off?
[09:30] Maya Chen: Will do. We'll produce pricing for Hosted pilot with store_request off and a Dedicated baseline for comparison.
[09:40] Aisha Khan: One final thing 

do you have a 'redaction preview' API for CI testing?
[09:44] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, we have an endpoint that returns a redacted preview for a sample payload; great for CI gating. We'll share doc link.
[10:00] Maya Chen: Recap: we'll send SOC2 + security pack, sample API calls and screenshots, and propose pilot plan. Rafael will share demo recording and screenshots. Customer to confirm pilot scope and internal POC.
[10:15] Priya Singh: Thanks. We'll look for those docs.
[10:18] Liam O'Connor: Thanks everyone.
[10:20] Maya Chen: Thanks, bye.
notes: Demo focused on per-route storage toggles, redaction rules, KMS support, and auditability. Customer wants legal/contract language and pilot to validate store_request=false. Some transcription artifacts present (e.g., K M S split), consistent with auto-transcribe.
